outcome: The general question (does strong mixing imply strong 3-mixing / mixing of all orders?) remains open, but Kanigowski and Ravotti (arXiv:2410.13686, Oct 2024) settled it affirmatively for a broad new class of parabolic systems by introducing 'locally uniformly shearing' (LUS) flows and proving all LUS flows are mixing of all orders, with Kochergin flows on the 2-torus and smooth time-changes of unipotent flows as consequences.
summary: The frozen Wikipedia bullet asks whether all strongly mixing systems are also strongly 3-mixing — Rokhlin's 1949 problem, still open in general as of today. Within the window, the clearest development is Kanigowski & Ravotti, 'Multiple mixing for parabolic systems' (arXiv:2410.13686, submitted 2024-10-17): they define 'locally uniformly shearing' (LUS) systems, formalizing the known 'mixing via shearing' mechanism behind essentially all known zero-entropy mixing examples, and prove every LUS flow is mixing of all orders (i.e. strongly mixing implies strongly k-mixing for all k within this class). They derive as corollaries that Kochergin flows on T^2 (for a.e. irrational frequency) and smooth time-changes of unipotent flows are polynomially mixing of all orders. This is a restriction of the stated question to a specific, well-motivated class of parabolic/zero-entropy systems, not a resolution of the general question, so I coded it `partial` with `resolution_direction: confirmed` (the settled case went the conjectured/expected way — mixing does imply multiple mixing there). I also read Ryzhikov's survey 'Multiple mixing, 75 years of Rokhlin's problem' (arXiv:2411.07234, submitted 2024-11-11), which explicitly states the general question 'remains open' after 75 years, catalogs the pre-existing classes where a positive answer was already known (singular spectrum, Ratner-property flows, positive local rank, finite rank automorphisms, Gaussian/Poisson suspensions) and the pre-2024 negative results for higher-dimensional actions (Ledrappier's Z^2 counterexample, predating the window), and cites a 2023 result of Ryzhikov's own on generic automorphisms deviating from multiple mixing — none of which are new results inside the window and none of which resolve the stated bullet. The survey does not mention the Kanigowski-Ravotti paper (likely a scheduling/overlap coincidence given the one-month gap between the two arXiv postings) or any AI/computer-assisted methods. I found no AI involvement anywhere in this area: no lab announcement, no author statement crediting a model with any part of either paper's mathematics, and no machine-checked or formalized proof. The current live Wikipedia list article's Rokhlin entry is worded identically to the frozen revision, consistent with the problem still being open in general.
competing_reading: One could argue the Kanigowski-Ravotti LUS result is close enough to 'the' answer that it deserves a stronger status than `partial`, since LUS captures essentially every known mechanism for zero-entropy mixing and the authors present it as unifying prior special-case results. But the stated bullet is the fully general question over all strongly mixing systems, and LUS is explicitly a sufficient condition, not a characterization — non-LUS mixing systems are not excluded from being counterexamples, so the general problem is unambiguously still open and `partial` is the correct scope-respecting call per §3.1.
what_would_settle_it: Either (a) a proof that every strongly mixing system is strongly 3-mixing (or a counterexample showing some strongly mixing but not 3-mixing Z-system, resolving the general problem), or (b) a proof that LUS (or some other checkable condition) is not just sufficient but necessary for multiple mixing, which would at least clarify how much territory the general problem still covers.

judgement.doubts: Agree with the record. The LUS result settles a class of systems (a restriction of the bullet), so it is a case, not whole; the general question stays open per Ryzhikov's survey. Two possibly relevant 2024 preprints (2405.03641, 2404.06476) were not opened by the researcher, and one of them is year-mid-2024 so it would be post-snapshot anyway; unlikely to change the tier.
